app.description: The app's own containers. A map of named parts; exactly one has public: true (the front door).

build.description: Build context — AppTown builds this repo's Dockerfile. Exactly one of build/image/static.

image.description: A pushed image reference to run as-is.

static.description: A static site, served by AppTown's own file server. A string is a committed folder, served as it is. A map builds the site first: the Dockerfile in build (its target stage, default the last) is built, and the folder output inside that stage's files is served.

build.description: Build context: the folder whose Dockerfile builds the site.

target.description: The Dockerfile stage holding the site (default: the last stage).

output.description: The folder inside that stage's files to serve, e.g. dist. No symbolic links are allowed in it.

command.description: Override the container command (compose form: string or list).

replicas.description: Instances of this app part. Omitted or null means 1. Only 1 is currently supported; larger counts are not supported and are refused by the contract validator before execution. Not a profile or init-container field.

ports.description: Compose-style ports; AppTown assigns the host port, so the container port is what matters (e.g. ["8080"]).

dataDir.description: A directory backed by a named volume that survives redeploys.

seed.description: Reserved. AppTown accepts this field but runs it nowhere: not in development, preview or deployment. Use an init step for a command that must run before the app starts.

healthcheck.description: Legacy: a shell command; exit 0 means healthy. Prefer health.

public.description: Marks the one front-door part the preview/deploy URL points at.

health.description: Structured health intent for this part (design/subsystems/healthchecks.md).

readiness.description: One probe. Exactly one target: http, tcp or exec.

tcp.description: A port; 0 infers it from the part.

exec.description: A command run inside the container.

requestContext.description: Readiness only: probe through the front door or the container directly.

expect.description: Readiness only: the HTTP status that means ready (default 200).

checksDeps.description: Readiness only: the app asserts this probe checks its dependencies. Recorded, not proven.

startupGrace.description: A duration with a unit, e.g. 90s. The minimum wait before failures count.

period.description: A duration with a unit, e.g. 10s.

timeout.description: A duration with a unit, e.g. 5s.

liveness.description: One probe. Exactly one target: http, tcp or exec.

exec.description: A command run inside the container.

expect.description: Readiness only: the HTTP status that means ready (default 200).

period.description: A duration with a unit, e.g. 10s.

timeout.description: A duration with a unit, e.g. 5s.

resources.description: The most this part may use. A part that declares nothing has no limit. A cap, not a reservation.

memory.description: Memory, swap included, in Kubernetes binary units: a whole number of Mi or Gi, at least 32Mi. E.g. 512Mi, 2Gi. A version-1 contract also reads M and G as MiB and GiB; version 2 refuses them.

cpu.description: A positive number of CPUs, e.g. 0.5 or 2, or Kubernetes millicores, e.g. 500m.

init.description: Ordered run-to-completion containers that must SUCCEED before the app parts start (migrations, asset builds). Maps to ECS containers the app dependsOn with condition SUCCESS.

build.description: Build context (usually '.', sharing the app image). Exactly one of build/image.

needs.description: Dependencies fulfilled per deployment from the catalog (postgres, s3, sso, ...). A map of capability -> parameters.

additionalProperties.description: Typed params (version, database, flow, ...) vary by capability; each is a single value. 'properties' is an escape hatch for esoteric provisioning params not modelled ahead of time.

properties.description: Escape hatch: arbitrary key/value provisioning params, passed through to fulfillment. Names are un-schema'd on purpose; each value is a single value.

resources.description: The most this need's service may use, as a part's resources. A need that declares nothing has no limit. Not a parameter: the catalogue never sees it. Refused for a need whose kind runs no service.

memory.description: Memory, swap included, in Kubernetes binary units: a whole number of Mi or Gi, at least 32Mi. E.g. 512Mi, 2Gi. A version-1 contract also reads M and G as MiB and GiB; version 2 refuses them.

cpu.description: A positive number of CPUs, e.g. 0.5 or 2, or Kubernetes millicores, e.g. 500m.

size.description: Catalogue-owned local-container size (needs only); cannot combine with resources.

version.description: The contract's shape version. 2 is current: memory in Mi or Gi only, and environment values may read a need's values as ${needs.<need>.<VARIABLE>} ($${needs. for the literal text). Absent means 1: M and G read as MiB and GiB, and environment values are delivered as written. A version AppTown does not know is an error, never a partial read.

secrets.description: What AppTown must know about the app's secrets beyond secretspec.toml.

spec.description: The secretspec file, secretspec.toml by default.

generate.description: Secrets AppTown generates, by name, with their stability domain.

deliver.description: How each named secret reaches the app. Only env is built.

rehearsal.description: What a restore rehearsal asks the app besides its readiness and its front page.

checks.description: Data checks: paths the app answers without its own sign-in that read its database, each "GET /path" or "GET /path expect <status>". AppTown records only the status each answers.

profiles.description: Named profiles. A deployment uses one profile (chosen per deployment, shared with secretspec.toml); previews use preview when declared. Each profile maps part and need names to what it changes: a part's resources and environment, a need's resources or catalogue size; resources replace the part's field by field, environment merges key by key. default is the parts themselves and is not declared here.

additionalProperties.description: Part or need name → what this profile changes of it (a need: resources or catalogue size).

resources.description: The most this part may use. A part that declares nothing has no limit. A cap, not a reservation.

memory.description: Memory, swap included, in Kubernetes binary units: a whole number of Mi or Gi, at least 32Mi. E.g. 512Mi, 2Gi. A version-1 contract also reads M and G as MiB and GiB; version 2 refuses them.

cpu.description: A positive number of CPUs, e.g. 0.5 or 2, or Kubernetes millicores, e.g. 500m.

environment.description: Environment merged over the part's own.

size.description: Catalogue-owned local-container size (needs only); cannot combine with resources.

allOf.description: Version 2 writes memory in Mi or Gi only.
